title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50 year old Tennessee woman, is suing the city of Fargo, North Dakota, and police detective Lucas Heck for $10m after she was falsely arrested and jailed for about six months. Police used AI facial recognition software that matched a fake ID photo from bank fraud surveillance footage to Lipps’s social media picture. She was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025, held nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition, then about two more months in North Dakota. Charges of theft and unauthorized use of personal identifying information were dropped after her lawyer provided bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time of the fraud.

Lipps was released on Christmas Eve with no way home and later learned she had lost her residence, car, and personal property. Her lawsuit alleges police lacked proper training and supervision for facial recognition technology and ignored the risk of wrongful detention. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. Lipps seeks accountability and hopes the case will make officers more careful when using AI facial recognition in criminal investigations.
